The system models these as stochastic processes in GSI’s Bayesian framework, where each row defines a conditional probability P(gate | risk_state). In GSE, these predicates trigger deterministic state transitions. For example, R_{pc} > threshold implies NO-GO, which is a hard constraint in a Markovian policy space. The dual nature of risk—both probabilistic and deterministic—creates a hybrid logic layer. Failure modes include misclassification of contests, lack of consent, and scoring ambiguity. These are modeled as singularities in the risk manifold, where small perturbations in input (e.g., missing consent) cause large shifts in outcome (NO-GO).
